page.layout: One page of text, set as verse in italic. Below the poem: the signed initials "I. I. B." right-aligned, then a printer's ornament. No margin notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right.

p.i: Victor splendidus obteris, Et tristi patriam funere liberas.
Heu!mens cæca cupidine Quum regni rapitur, quo ruit impetu Præceps per vetitum nefas?
Nullum turpe putat flagitium, aut scelus, Leges iuraque[?] negligit, Cælesti arbitrio cuncta negans regi.
Nullos illa deos, neque Plectendis metuit Tartara sontibus.
Fertur filia mortuum Conculcasse ferox Tullia Seruium Bigis, dum properat patris Regem cæde sui cernere coniugem.
Regno fraudibus impiis Dauidem pepulit filius Absalom.
Quem mox dextera Numinis Feriens ætherei perdidit exitu Tristi, qui manet improbos Conatus meritum supplicium ferens.

page.notes: Ornament (printer's flower piece) below the signature, not transcribed. Faint mirrored text on the right and a faint word at lower left are show-through from the other side and were left out. "iuraque" has a doubtful accent over the a, marked [?]. The printed word "Dauidem" and the spellings are as printed.
